question: On one fixed upper-half-plane z box and Q>=4 at p=0, do the raw-C coefficient and its principal square-root branch remain separated from the nonpositive-real cut with a strictly positive real-part lower bound?

convention_provenance.role: pins the raw-C nonreal fiber coefficient convention only; it is not evidence for this outward branch audit

primary_sources.title: Weyl-Titchmarsh Theory for Sturm-Liouville Operators with Distributional Potentials
primary_sources.role: singular Weyl--Titchmarsh definition and nonreal-domain scope only; no model-specific endpoint or spectral theorem is imported

declared_conventions.execution: outward python-flint acb/arb elementary arithmetic at Q=4 plus exact half-line envelope; no ODE, root solver, quadrature, sample grid, boundary map, or characteristic equation

controls: Exact factorization and the strictly negative derivative d exp(-Q/2)/dQ=-exp(-Q/2)/2 prove that the Q=4 box bounds every Q>=4.

At both 128 and 256 bits, same-backend outward acb arithmetic must give finite delta, relative-factor, A and principal-sqrt rectangles with |delta|<1, cut distance positive, and Re sqrt(A)>0; the two rectangles must overlap as a consistency check, not independent evidence.
Executable exact SymPy inequalities sqrt(290)/16<9/8, exp(-2)<1/7 and pi^2>9 give |delta|<1/336 and cut distance >335/336; every ball bound must be no weaker than this sufficient separation test.
